sentences.text: Bernissartia was a neosuchian crocodyliform that lived during the Early Cretaceous, approximately 130 million years ago.
This animal reached a total length of only 60 cm, marking it as one of the smallest crocodyliforms in history.
It was probably semi-aquatic and resembled modern crocodilians in many respects.
Its mouth featured long, pointed front teeth for catching fish alongside broad, flat back teeth for crushing hard foods like shellfish and bones.
The genus is named after the Belgian locality of Bernissart where its remains were discovered.
The genus was described by Dollo in 1883.
Primary fossil evidence comes from skulls and skeletons found in the Sainte-Barbe Clays Formation of Belgium and the Camarillas Formation of Spain.
Bernissartia belongs to the family Bernissartiidae.
Research suggests that Bernissartia is not technically a modern crocodile (Eusuchia) according to phylogenetic analyses by Larsson & Sues (2007) and Sereno et al. (2003).
Fossils of Bernissartia date from the Kimmeridgian to the Cenomanian stages, between 152.21 and 93.9 million years ago.
